# Blue Nebula product brief

November 2026 · Product concept and proposed requirements

Blue Nebula is the working name for the Local First AI Engineering Operating System described in the project PRD. It is an application layer connecting a repository, editable visual canvas, persistent project memory, model runtimes, and a permissioned action system.

## The intended audience

Start with independent developers and designers who implement interfaces, using Windows 11 x64, VS Code, and React with TypeScript. Small studio coordination follows demonstrated demand.

## The core journey

1. Resume an authorized project using branch-aware, cited decisions and current task context.
2. Create and edit a supported interface on a structured native canvas.
3. Inspect the resulting code patch and preserve concurrent manual edits.
4. Observe scoped actions and run declared verification checks.
5. Review artifacts, evidence, remaining limitations, and proposed memory updates.

## Product principles

- Local inference and storage by default, with a supported offline workflow after installation.
- Cloud use and consequential external actions require separate permissions.
- Memory has provenance, scope, lifecycle, correction, deletion, and readable exports.
- Completion requires observed evidence; missing or failing checks do not count as passed.
- Improve retrieval and workflows before offering optional, separately consented adaptation.

## Proposed hardware profiles

- H0: Windows 11 x64, 16 GB RAM, SSD, CPU inference. Memory and canvas are intended to remain usable; small-model inference is best effort. No speed guarantee.
- H1: 32 GB RAM, 12 GB NVIDIA VRAM, NVMe SSD, 30 GB free after model installation. Proposed reference for one compact model, retrieval, and one task. Exact model requires qualification.
- H2: 64 GB RAM, 24 GB NVIDIA VRAM, 100 GB free, supported isolated Linux training environment. For later optional small adapter jobs only; certification required.

## Proposed phases

Foundation: local feasibility trials, memory, canvas, patches, policy controls, and evidence.
Connection: scoped reverse synchronization, portable projects, and qualified desktop adapters.
Collaboration: explicit project sharing, roles, and review.
Adaptation: lawful reviewed data, separate consent, held-out evaluation, reversible adapter promotion.

No release dates, measured product results, customer endorsements, certifications, or comparative advantage have been established.

## About the website demonstration

The browser demo contains an editable card, generated JSX, searchable authored example decisions, a deterministic guided workflow, and real local fixture checks. It makes no AI calls, connects no repository, and does not execute the generated component. The checks validate demo data and generated text, not compilation or product security. Canvas preferences are saved only in this browser when available. Downloads are generated locally.

The desktop application described by the PRD is not included in this landing-page implementation. There is no shipping installer or backend signup service on this site.
